title: Cross-attention conditioning
goal:
Section 3.3 conditions the U-Net with a cross-attention layer: queries come from the U-Net's features $\phi_i(z_t)$, and keys and values come from the encoded condition $\tau_\theta(y)$.

Write `cross_attention(phi, tau, W_Q, W_K, W_V)`, which returns `(output, weights)`.

- `phi` has shape `(N, d_eps)`: one row per spatial position of the flattened U-Net feature map.
- `tau` has shape `(M, d_tau)`: one row per condition token.
- `W_Q` has shape `(d, d_eps)`, and `W_K` and `W_V` have shape `(d, d_tau)`. Use $Q = \phi W_Q^\top$ and likewise for $K$ and $V$.
- `weights` has shape `(N, M)` and each row sums to 1. `output` has shape `(N, d)`.

The paper prints the shapes of $W_Q$ and $W_V$ the other way round. The shapes above are the only ones that make the products defined.
hints: The scores are `Q @ K.T`, with shape `(N, M)`. Divide by $\sqrt{d}$, where $d$ is the projection width.
Each query chooses among condition tokens, so the softmax runs over the last axis, the `M` tokens.
The output is `weights @ V`. It has one row per image position, never one per token.
